steps.text: For this recipe, the Monsieur Cuisine "Steamer basket" is required.
Wash 80 g of untreated lime with hot water, pat dry, peel off the zest, halve the lime, and squeeze out the juice.
Add half of the zest and half of the juice to a small bowl.
Add 15 g of olive oil to the bowl.
Add 5 g of honey to the bowl.
Season to taste with salt and pepper, and mix.

Add the roasted hazelnuts to the blender jug.
Adapted cooking

Add 1 cold egg (small).

Add 1/2 tsp lemon zest.
Basic kneading
Roll the dough into a ball and wrap in cling film. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
Grease the springform tin and preheat the oven to 180 °C (top and bottom heat).
Remove one third of the dough and immediately return it to the refrigerator.
Place the remaining dough in the springform tin and use your hands or a small rolling pin to form a base.
Spoon 165 g redcurrant jam into a small bowl and stir until smooth.
Spread evenly on the cake base, leaving a 1.5 cm border all around.
Take a quarter of the remaining dough, and set aside.
On a floured surface, shape the remaining dough into 8 rolls, 1 cm in diameter and 17 cm long.
Slightly flatten these and arrange in a lattice pattern over the jam.
Trim off any overhanging dough, ensuring that the jam-free edge remains free.
Shape the dough trimmings along with the reserved dough into a slightly thicker roll.
Slightly flatten again and place in a circle on the jam-free outer cake edge.
Put 1 egg yolk (small) in a small bowl.
Add 5 g milk (UHT, 3.5% fat) to the egg yolk, and whisk.
Brush the dough lattice and the edge with the egg yolk-milk mixture.
Weigh out 35 g flaked almonds in a separate bowl.
Sprinkle the dough border with the flaked almonds and press them down gently.
Bake the cake in the preheated oven for 40 minutes.
Once the jam begins to simmer between the dough lattice, the cake is done.
Remove the cake from the oven, let cool on a wire rack for 30 minutes, and carefully remove from the tin.
Let the cake cool completely and serve sprinkled with the remaining icing sugar.

steps.text: Wash 40 g herbs of your choice, shake dry and tear the leaves from the stalks.
If you use rosemary or chives, it would be easier to chop by hand. Put the herb leaves into the blender jug.
Step
Use the spatula to scrape the herbs down the inside of the blender jug and carry out the next step if required; otherwise, skip it.
Step
Remove the chopped leaves and rinse out the blender jug.
Rinse 600 g pork fillets under cold running water and pat dry.
Remove any fat, tendons and silver skin.
Cut the meat into two equally sized pieces, brush with 20 g olive oil and then toss in the herbs until they are completely covered.
Put each piece of pork into a vacuum bag and vacuum seal.
Alternatively, put the pork in 2 freezer bags.
Place the freezer bags in water with their openings pointing upwards and press the air out of them completely, then seal them tight with clips.
Insert the cooking pot into the blender jug and fill the blender jug with hot tap water up to just below the edge of the cooking pot.
Step
Place the vacuum-sealed pork fillets in the cooking pot and press them gently into the water until they are completely covered.
If the pork fillets are in freezer bags, place them in the cooking pot so that the opening, closed with the clip, is pointing upwards.
If necessary, pour in a little more water, but be careful not to go over the maximum fill level of the blender jug.
During the next step, after 1 hour, pre-heat the oven to 50 °C (top and bottom heat) and start preparing the vegetables on the stove.
Adapted cooking
Peel, wash and halve or quarter 800 g waxy potatoes, depending on their size.
Put the potatoes into a pot and add water until they are covered. Add 1 tsp salt and cook the potatoes for 15–20 minutes.
Then drain, decant into a bowl and mix with 15 g butter. Keep warm in the oven.
Peel and wash 700 g carrots.
Put plenty of water and 1 tsp salt in a large pot and bring to the boil. Add the carrots and cook for 7 minutes over a high heat, then drain thoroughly.
Heat 50 g butter in a pan.
Add 10 g brown sugar and, while stirring the mixture, allow to lightly caramelise.
Put the carrots in the pan and fry them on all sides.
Sprinkle the carrots with ½ tsp herb salt and the parsley and place them in the oven to keep warm.
After the pork fillets have cooked, remove the cooking pot from the blender jug, take the pork fillets out of the vacuum bags and reserve the cooking liquid.
Pat the pork fillets dry carefully so that the herbs will not come off.
Sprinkle with ½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper on all sides and place them in the oven to keep warm.
Empty the blender jug.
Peel and halve 100 g onions and put the pieces in the blender jug.
Step
Use the spatula to push the mixture down the inside of the blender jug.
Put 30 g butter into the blender jug.
Remove the measuring beaker from the lid.
Step
Add 30 g plain flour (type 405) to the blender jug.
Add 10 g tomato purée.
Step
Add 100 g of the reserved cooking liquid to the blender jug.
Add 200 g beef stock. (Depending on how much cooking liquid you have reserved, add a little more or less beef stock, so that the total amount of liquid is 300 g.)
Add 100 g cream (30% fat).
Add 10 g Worcestershire sauce.
Add ¼ tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper.
Insert the measuring beaker into the lid.
Step
Remove the measuring beaker into the lid.
Step
Cut the pork fillets into slices 2 cm thick and serve with the potatoes, the caramelised carrots and the sauce.

recipes.title: Sous-vide caramelised pineapple with walnut ice cream
recipes.author: Monsieur Cuisine Official

steps.text: Mode

recipes.title: Sous-vide caramelised pineapple with walnut ice cream
recipes.author: Monsieur Cuisine Official

steps.text: Bring 200 g milk (fresh milk, 3.5% fat) and 200 g cream (30% fat) to room temperature.
Put 200 g room-temperature milk (fresh whole milk, 3.5% fat) in the blender jug.
Add 200 g room-temperature cream (30% fat).
Add 80 g sugar.
Add 2 egg yolks (medium).
Add 1 tsp vanilla paste.
Add 1 pinch of salt.
Mode
Decant the milk and cream mixture into a shallow bowl lined with clingfilm.
Leave to cool, then freeze for at least 5 hours (ideally overnight) in the freezer.
Brown 60 g walnuts in a frying pan on a medium heat, until they release their nutty aroma. Decant and leave to cool.
Turn out the ice cream mixture, cut it into 3-cm cubes and put them in the blender jug.
Mode
Put the walnuts in the blender jug.
Mode
Put the ice cream back into the bowl and freeze for another 2 hours.
Peel 1 pineapple (1400 g) and remove the eyes.
Cut the flesh into 2-cm-thick slices, remove the stalk, then cut the slices into quarters.
Put the pineapple pieces in the vacuum bag, ideally close together, and remove the air. Alternatively, you could put the pineapple in a freezer bag.
Place the freezer bag in the water with the opening pointing upwards and press the air out of it completely, then seal it tight with a clip.
Insert the cooking pot into the blender jug and full the blender jug with hot tap water up to just below the edge of the cooking pot.
Mode
Place the vacuum-sealed pineapple pieces in the cooking pot and press them gently into the water until they are completely covered.
If the pineapple pieces are in a freezer bag, place it in the cooking pot so that the opening, closed with the clip, is pointing upwards.
If necessary, pour in a little more water, but be careful not to go over the maximum fill level of the blender jug.
Mode
Then remove the vacuum bag from the blender jug, take out the pineapple pieces and pat them dry with kitchen paper.
Sprinkle the pineapple pieces with ½ tsp cinnamon and 30 g brown sugar, then caramelise them with 20 g butter in a pan.
Serve the pineapple pieces with the walnut ice cream.

recipes.title: Sous-vide corn-fed chicken breast with herbs and cinnamon ratatouille
recipes.author: Monsieur Cuisine Official

steps.text: Mode

recipes.title: Sous-vide corn-fed chicken breast with herbs and cinnamon ratatouille
recipes.author: Monsieur Cuisine Official

steps.text: Wash 4 corn-fed chicken breasts (skin on, 150 g each) under cold running water and pat dry.
Wash 1 unwaxed lemon (150 g) and pat dry.
Use a peeler to remove 4 strips of rind from the lemon and set aside.
Squeeze the lemon and reserve the juice.
Wash 12 basil leaves, 2 sprigs of oregano and 1 sprig of rosemary and pat dry.
Carefully push 3 basil leaves under the skin of each chicken breast.
Peel 3 garlic cloves, squash them gently with the back of a knife and put them into a bowl.

Add 3 tbsp olive oil, 2 bay leaves, 2 sprigs of oregano, 1 sprig of rosemary and
2 strips of lemon peel and mix together.
Put the marinade and chicken breasts into a vacuum bag and vacuum seal. Alternatively, put the chicken breasts and the marinade in freezer bags.
Place the freezer bags in water with their openings pointing upwards and press the air out of them completely, then seal them tight with clips.
Leave the chicken breasts to infuse for at least 2 hours. Meanwhile, prepare the vegetables for the cinnamon ratatouille.

Peel 1 small red onion
(60 g), cut it into quarters, chop roughly and set aside.
Peel 3 garlic cloves, squash them gently with the back of a knife and set aside.
Cut 2 small red peppers (270 g) into quarters, remove the cores and wash them inside and out.
Cut the peppers into 2-cm pieces, discarding the stalks, and set aside.

Wash and trim 1 courgette
(230 g), cut it into rough chunks and set aside.

Wash and trim
½ aubergine (150 g), cut it into rough chunks and set aside.
Wash and trim 3 large tomatoes (340 g), cut them into rough chunks and set aside.
Wash and dry 4 sprigs of thyme and set aside.
Insert the cooking pot into the blender jug and fill the blender jug with hot tap water up to just below the edge of the cooking pot.
Put the lid on the blender jug.
Prepare the vegetable stock (250 ml) just before the end of the following step.
Mode
Note: the next 5 steps must be carried out at the same time as the sous-vide cooking of the chicken breasts.
Pre-heat the oven to 170 °C (top and bottom heat).
Heat 3 tbsp vegetable oil in a casserole dish and sweat the onion.
Add the roughly chopped vegetables, thyme, garlic cloves, the remaining strips of lemon peel and 2 cinnamon sticks and sauté briefly.

Stir in 1 tbsp tomato purée, then deglaze with 250 ml hot vegetable stock and
3 tbsp lemon juice.
Season with 1 tsp salt and ½ tsp pepper, cover and stew the cinnamon ratatouille in the preheated oven for 40 minutes.
Place the vacuum-sealed chicken breasts in the cooking pot and press them gently into the water until they are completely covered.
If the chicken breasts are in freezer bags, place them in the cooking pot so that their openings, closed with the clips, are pointing upwards.
If necessary, pour in a little more water, but be careful not to go over the maximum fill level of the blender jug.
Mode
Take the bag out of the blender jug. Carefully remove the chicken breasts from the bags and pat dry.
Heat 1 tbsp butter and 2 tbsp vegetable oil in a frying pan and fry the meat until crispy, first on the skin side and then on the other side.
Remove the cinnamon stick, lemon peel and herb sprigs from the ratatouille. Season to taste with salt, pepper and lemon juice.
Serve the chicken breasts with the cinnamon ratatouille.

recipes.author: Monsieur Cuisine Official

steps.text: Pre-heat the oven to 170 °C (top and bottom heat).
Wash 500 g lamb fillets under cold running water and pat dry.

Brush the lamb fillets with 2 tbsp olive oil and season with 1 tsp fennel seeds,
1 tsp coriander seeds, ½ tsp salt and
½ tsp pepper.
Wash 6 sage leaves, shake them dry, put them into a vacuum bag along with the lamb fillets and vacuum seal.
Alternatively, put the lamb fillets and the sage leaves in freezer bags.
Place the freezer bags in water with their openings pointing upwards and press the air out of them completely, then seal them tight with clips.

Wash 4 aubergines
(1200 g), dry them and cut them in half.
Season the cut sides of the aubergines with ½ tsp salt and ½ tsp pepper.
Place the aubergines on a baking sheet, cut side down, and drizzle over 4 tbsp olive oil.
Bake in the pre-heated oven for 1 hour.
Wash 2 sprigs of rosemary and 4 sage leaves and shake them dry.
Wash 16 cherry tomatoes (300 g), shake them dry and set aside.
Peel 4 garlic cloves and squash them gently with the back of a knife.
Put the herbs and garlic cloves in a pot with 200 ml room-temperature olive oil and heat up.
Insert the cooking pot into the blender jug and fill the blender jug with hot tap water up to just below the edge of the cooking pot.
Put the lid on the blender jug.
Mode
Place the vacuum-sealed lamb fillets in the cooking pot and press them gently into the water until they are completely covered.
If the lamb fillets are in freezer bags, place them in the cooking pot so that their openings, closed with the clips, are pointing upwards.

Mode

recipes.author: Monsieur Cuisine Official

steps.text: Grease a casserole dish with butter.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C (top and bottom heat).
Place 30 g of pitted black olives in a sieve, and drain.
Drain 30 g of sun-dried tomatoes on kitchen paper.
Peel, wash, and slice 500 g of waxy potatoes with a vegetable slicer or knife into thin slices. Layer them in the prepared casserole dish.
Remove the rind from 30 g of Parmesan (32 % fat) and add in 2 cm pieces to the blender jug.
Adapted cooking
Transfer the Parmesan.
Rinse the blender jug.
Peel 1 garlic clove and add to the blender jug.
Press the turbo button for 2 seconds.
Push down with the spatula.
Add 200 g of cold cream (30% fat) to the blender jug.
Add 100 g of cold milk (UHT, 3.5% fat).
Add 1 tsp salt and 2 pinches of ground black pepper.
Halve the olives, and add.
Cut the sun-dried tomatoes into strips, and add.
Adapted cooking
Perform the following steps during the next step.
Pour the sauce over the potatoes, sprinkle with Parmesan, and bake in the oven for 45 minutes until golden brown. Check if the potatoes are cooked; if not, extend the baking time by a few minutes.
Clean the blender jug.
Wash 1 rosemary stem and 1 thyme sprig, shake dry, and place in the vacuum bag.
Rinse 400 g of lamb fillets under cold running water, pat dry, and add to the herbs. Vacuum seal.
Alternatively, put the lamb fillets in a freezer bag.
Place the freezer bag in water with the opening facing upwards, press out all the air, and seal tightly with a clip.
Place the cooking pot into the blender jug and fill the blender jug with hot water just below the upper rim of the cooking pot.
Adapted cooking
Place the vacuum-sealed bag in the cooking pot and gently press it into the water until completely submerged.
Freezer bags should be placed in the cooking pot so that the bag opening with the clips faces upwards.
If necessary, add more hot water, while observing the maximum fill level of the blender jug.
Adapted cooking
Remove the vacuum bag from the cooking pot and set aside. Remove the cooking pot and empty the blender jug.
Carefully remove the lamb fillets from the bag and pat them thoroughly dry.
Briefly sear the meat on each side in a hot pan with 30 g clarified butter. Season with 1/2 tsp of salt and 1 pinch of ground black pepper.
Portion out the lamb fillets with the potato gratin onto two plates, and serve.

Then smooth it out and make 3 more Parmesan crisps with the rest of the Parmesan.
Put the baking sheet with the Parmesan crisps in the oven for 2 minutes, so that the Parmesan melts. Take them out of the oven and leave them to cool.
Trim 300 g porcini, cut them into bite-sized pieces and set aside.

Mode

recipes.author: Monsieur Cuisine Official

steps.text: Peel and quarter 1 onion (70 g) and put it into the blender jug.
Roughly chop 150 g smoked bacon and add to the blender jug.
Mode
Use the spatula to scrape down the inside of the blender jug.
Put 1 tbsp vegetable oil into the blender jug.

Mode

Add 300 g warm water.
Mode
Decant the broth into a bowl and leave it to stand at room temperature for at least 30 minutes, until it is lukewarm.
Meanwhile, leave the salmon to stand at room temperature.
Rinse 4 salmon fillets (125 g each) under cold running water and pat them dry.
Leave the salmon to marinate in the broth for 2 hours.
Now carefully vacuum seal the salmon with a little of the smoked broth, then set aside. Alternatively, put the salmon fillets and a little smoked broth in freezer bags.
Place the freezer bags in water with their openings pointing upwards and press the air out of them completely, then seal them tight with clips.

steps.text: Wash 2 apples (400 g), cut them into quarters and discard the cores.

Add 1 tsp raisins, 4 cardamom seeds, 1 tsp black peppercorns, 1 bay leaf, 2 tsp sugar, 1 cinnamon stick and 2 juniper berries and mix together.
Put the apple and spice mixture into a vacuum bag and vacuum seal. Alternatively, put theapple and spice mixture in a freezer bag.
Place the freezer bag in the water with the opening pointing upwards and press the air out of it completely, then seal it tight with a clip.
Insert the cooking pot into the blender jug and fill the blender jug with hot tap water up to just below the edge of the cooking pot.
Put the lid on the blender jug.
Mode
Place the vacuum-sealed apple sticks in the cooking pot and press them gently into the water until they are completely covered.
If the apple sticks are in a freezer bag, place it in the cooking pot so that the opening, closed with the clip, is pointing upwards.
If necessary, pour in a little more hot water, but be careful not to go over the maximum fill level of the blender jug.
Mode
Remove the vacuum bag, cut it open and transfer the contents to a pot.
Add 1 tsp red peppercorns and 1 tsp vinegar.
Add 100 g apple juice at room temperature and bring everything to a boil briefly.
Empty out the blender jug, rinse with cold water and insert the mixer attachment.
Pour 100 g wheat beer at room temperature into the blender jug.
Add 60 g sugar.
Add 4 egg yolks (medium).
Mode
Leave the spiced apples to cool, then serve with the wheat beer zabaglione.

steps.text: Wash 6 medium-sized waxy potatoes (800 g) and put them in the cooking pot.
Pour 500 g hot water into the cooking pot.

Hang the cooking pot inside the blender jug.
Mode
Remove the cooking pot, allow the potatoes to release their steam for 15 minutes, peel and then allow to cool down completely for 8 hours overnight.
Empty the blender jug and rinse out.
Wash 4 Savoy cabbage leaves (130 g) and remove the hard leaf veins.
Place the still-damp leaves in the deep steamer basket.
Pour 1000 g hot water into the blender jug.
Place the deep steamer basket on top of the blender jug and close the lid.
Mode
Remove the deep steamer basket, rinse the cabbage leaves in cold water and drain well.
Empty the blender jug.
Coarsely grate the potatoes from the day before (e.g. on the coarse side of a square grater).
Heat 1 tbsp clarified butter in a large non-stick frying pan.
Add the grated potato and fry on a high heat, turning regularly, for 5 minutes until they are lightly browned.
Then, using a spatula, push everything towards the middle of the pan to make a compact shape while also pressing down well from above.
On a medium heat fry the grated potatoes on one side for 10 minutes until crispy and brown.
Place a plate the same size as the pan face down on top of the fried potatoes, carefully turn the pan and plate over and turn the potatoes out onto the plate.
Heat 1 tbsp of clarified butter in the frying pan, then slide the fried potatoes with the pale side facing down back into the pan.
Fry the underside for 10 minutes on a medium heat until crispy and brown.
Season the fried potatoes with ¼ tsp salt and 2 pinches of pepper and keep warm.
Beat 4 veal olives from the topside (170 g each) flat between 2 layers of cling film.
Season the meat with ½ teaspoon of salt and ¼ teaspoon of pepper each.
Cut the cabbage leaves in half lengthways and cover each veal roulade with 2 half leaves each.
Roll up the meat tightly, folding the long sides in towards the centre, wrap with kitchen twine and knot.
Heat 2 tbsp clarified butter in a frying pan and cook the veal roulades in it thoroughly on all sides on a high heat for 4 minutes.
Remove the meat and place in the deep steamer basket.
Deglaze the meat sediment with 400 g veal stock at room temperature and briefly bring to the boil to loosen it from the bottom of the pan.
Pour the liquid out of the frying pan into the blender jug.
Add 600 g hot water.
Attach the deep steamer basket to the blender jug and close the lid.
Mode
Check to see whether the roulades are cooked and carry out the next step if necessary; otherwise, skip it.
Mode

Remove the steamer basket and keep the roulades in a warm place.
Empty the blender jug, reserving the liquid.
Pour 400 g stock back into the blender jug.

Add 1 tsp lemon juice, 1 small pinch of nutmeg, 1 small pinch of pepper and the thyme.
Remove the measuring beaker from the lid.

Insert the measuring beaker into the lid.

steps.text: Mode
Wash 6 medium-sized waxy potatoes (800 g) and put them into the cooking pot.
Put 500 g hot water into the blender jug.
Add 1 tsp salt and ½ tsp caraway.
Attach the cooking pot to the blender jug.
Steam
Remove the cooking pot, allow the potatoes to release their steam for 15 minutes, peel and then allow to cool down completely for 8 hours and rest.
Empty out and dry the blender jug.
Next day, wash ½ bunch of flat-leaf parsley, shake it dry, tear the leaves from the stalks and put them into the blender jug.
Adapted cooking
Decant and rinse out the blender jug.
Pre-heat the oven to 60 °C (top and bottom heat).
Rinse 4 veal escalopes (150 g each) under cold running water and pat dry.
Remove any fat and tendons, and cut the veal into strips 1.5 cm thick and 4 cm long.
Heat up 1 tbsp of clarified butter in a large pan and, over a high heat, sear the meat all over in two batches, for 4 minutes each.
Transfer the meat to a bowl, leaving the cooking fat in the pan.
Season the meat with ½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper and put in the pre-heated oven to keep warm.
Trim 200 g button mushrooms and rub them dry with kitchen towel if necessary.
Cut the mushrooms into 0.5-cm-thick slices and arrange them in the shallow steamer basket.
Peel and halve 1 large onion (100 g) and put it into the blender jug.
Adapted cooking
Use the spatula to scrape down the inside of the blender jug.
Put 1 tbsp clarified butter into the blender jug.
Adapted cooking
Remove the measuring beaker from the lid.
Roast
Sprinkle 1 tbsp plain flour (type 405) over the onions in the blender jug.
Insert the measuring beaker into the lid.
Adapted cooking
Coarsely grate the potatoes from the day before (e.g. on the coarse side of a box grater).
Heat 1 tbsp clarified butter in a large non-stick frying pan.
Add the grated potato and fry on a high heat, turning regularly, for 5 minutes until it is lightly browned.
Then, using a spatula, push the potato towards the middle of the pan to make a compact rösti, while also pressing down firmly from above.
On a medium heat, fry the rösti on one side for 10 minutes until crispy and brown.
Using a plate the same size as the pan, place it face down on top of the rösti, carefully turn the pan and plate and turn the rösti out onto the plate.
Heat 1 tbsp clarified butter in the frying pan.
Slide the fried potatoes with the pale side facing down back into the pan and fry the underside for 10 minutes on a medium heat until crispy and brown.
Season the rösti with ¼ tsp salt and 2 pinches of pepper, then transfer to the pre-heated oven to keep warm.
Add 400 g room-temperature veal stock in the pan to the cooking fat and bring to boil briefly, stirring constantly, to loosen everything from the base of the pan.
Put the veal stock and cooking fat mixture in the blender jug.
Put 100 g dry white wine at room temperature into the blender jug.
Insert the shallow steamer basket containing the mushrooms into the deep steamer basket, attach to the blender jug and close the lid.
Adapted cooking
Remove the steamer attachment and set it aside, still closed.
Put 100 g room-temperature cream (at least 30% fat) into the blender jug.
Add the veal strips.
Add ¼ tsp salt, 1 big pinch each of pepper and nutmeg, and 1 tbsp lemon juice.
Adapted cooking
Place a bowl on top of the blender jug and weigh 20 g cornflour into it.
Weigh in 30 g cold water.
Stir the cornflour and water together until smooth, then add the mixture to the blender jug.
Remove the measuring beaker from the lid.
Adapted cooking
If desired, season the sauce to taste with salt and pepper.
Adapted cooking
Put the meat and sauce in a large serving dish, add the button mushrooms and mix everything together carefully.
Divide the rösti into four. Scatter the parsley over the sauce and serve the Zurich-style ragout with the rösti.
Wash 400 g waxy potatoes and place in the cooking pot.
Add 500 g hot water to the blender jug.
Add 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp whole caraway seeds.
Place the cooking pot into the blender jug.
Steam
Remove the cooking pot, let the potatoes stand for 15 minutes, peel, and leave to cool off completely for 8 hours.
Empty and dry the blender jug.
Remove the white wine from the refrigerator.
Wash 4 flat-leafed parsley sprigs, shake dry, pluck the leaves from the stems, and put in the blender jug.
Adapted cooking
Transfer, and rinse the blender jug.
Preheat the oven to 60 °C (top and bottom heat).
Rinse 300 g veal cutlets under cold running water and pat dry.
If necessary, remove fat and sinews from the meat and cut into 1.5 cm-thick and 4 cm-wide strips.
Heat 10 g clarified butter in a large pan and sear the meat on all sides for 4 minutes over high heat.
Transfer the meat to a bowl – leaving the pan drippings in the pan.
Season the meat with 1/4 tsp salt and a big pinch of ground black pepper, and keep warm in the preheated oven.
Clean 100 g white button mushrooms and wipe dry with kitchen paper if necessary.
Cut the mushrooms into 0.5 cm-thick slices and place in the cooking pot.
Peel and halve 50 g onions and put in the blender jug.
Adapted cooking
Scrape down with the spatula.
Add 10 g clarified butter to the blender jug.
Adapted cooking
Remove the measuring beaker from the lid.
Roast
Sprinkle 10 g plain flour (type 405) over the onions in the blender jug.
Insert the measuring beaker into the lid.
Adapted cooking
Coarsely grate the potatoes from the day before (using, for example, the coarse side of a box grater).
Heat 10 g clarified butter in a large non-stick pan.
Add the grated potatoes and fry for 5 minutes over high heat, turning them regularly, until lightly browned.
Using a spatula, push the potatoes towards the center of the pan to form a compact rösti, pressing down firmly on the potato mixture from above as well.
Fry the rösti on one side for 10 minutes over medium heat until crispy and browned.
Place a plate the size of the pan upside down on the rösti, carefully flip the pan with the plate, and unmold the rösti onto the plate.
Heat 10 g clarified butter in the pan.
Slide the rösti back into the pan with the lighter side down and fry the second side for 10 minutes over medium heat until crispy and browned.
Sprinkle the rösti with 1 pinch each of salt and ground black pepper and keep warm in the preheated oven.
Add 200 g room-temperature veal stock to the pan with the pan drippings and, while stirring, bring to a quick boil, to loosen the drippings from the base of the pan.
Add the veal stock with the pan drippings to the blender jug.
Add 50 g room-temperature dry white wine to the blender jug.
Place the cooking pot with the mushrooms into the blender jug.
Adapted cooking
Remove the cooking pot and keep warm.
Add 50 g cold cream (30% fat) to the blender jug.
Add the sliced veal.
Add 2 pinches of salt and 1 pinch each of ground black pepper and ground nutmeg.
Add 5 g lemon juice.
Adapted cooking
Place a bowl on the blender jug and weigh out 10 g cornflour.
Weigh out 15 g cold water.
Mix cornflour with water until smooth and add to the blender jug.
Remove the measuring beaker from the lid.
Adapted cooking
Season the sauce again to taste with salt and ground black pepper.
Adapted cooking
Transfer the sauce with the meat to a large serving bowl, add the mushrooms, and carefully mix everything together.
Cut the rösti into two pieces. Sprinkle the sauce with parsley and serve the Zürich-style sliced veal with the rösti.

steps.text: Mode

items.name: piping bag with large star nozzle

steps.text: Soak 4 leaves of gelatine according to the packet instructions.
Insert the mixer attachment into the blender jug.
Add 200 g chilled cream (30% fat).
Keep a constant eye on the jug while carrying out the next step and interrupt or extend the process as necessary.
Customized
Decant the cream and clean the blender jug.
Dissolve the gelatine in a small saucepan on a low heat. Remove the saucepan from the hob.
Stir a few tablespoons of cream into the gelatine, then gradually fold this mixture evenly into the remaining cream. Chill in the refrigerator.
Mix 1 sachet of blancmange powder and 50 g sugar in a small bowl.
Place a container on top of the blender jug and weigh 375 g chilled milk (fresh whole milk, 3.5% fat) into it.
Take 6 tbsp of chilled milk from this quantity and stir into the blancmange powder until smooth.
Insert the mixer attachment into the blender jug.
Pour the remaining milk into the blender jug.
Customized
Put the blancmange powder paste into the mixing bowl.
Customized
Remove the measuring beaker from the lid.
Customized
Decant into a large bowl, cover with cling film directly on top of the mixture and chill in the refrigerator.
Clean the blender jug.
Put 250 g water at room temperature into the blender jug.
Add 60 g butter in pieces.
Add 1 pinch of salt.
Insert the measuring beaker into the lid.
Customized
Add 150 g plain flour (type 405).
Customized
Allow the blender jug to cool down uncovered for 10 minutes.
Pre-heat the oven to 200 °C (top and bottom heat).
Remove the measuring beaker from the lid.
During the next step, add 4 eggs (medium) one by one through the lid opening and stir until there is a smooth consistency.
Customized
Insert the measuring beaker into the lid.
Customized
Allow the dough to cool down uncovered for 10 minutes.
Decant the dough mixture into a piping bag with large nozzle.
Keeping a distance between them, pipe 15 strips of dough about 10 cm long on 2 baking sheets lined with greaseproof paper.
Bake the sheets one after the other in the oven for 20 minutes until golden. Do not open the oven door during baking.
In the meantime, stir through the blancmange and cream using a dough scraper, then fold the cream into the blancmange with the dough scraper.
Decant the mixture into a piping bag with a large star nozzle and chill again.
Remove the golden, risen strips of dough from the oven and let them cool down completely on the baking sheet for at least 30 minutes.
Carefully cut through the dough strips horizontally. Arrange the lids with the cut side down on a strip of greaseproof paper.
For the topping, heat the cake glaze according to packet instructions.
Brush the pastry lids with it. Pipe a little vanilla cream onto the lower halves of the pastry strips and place the lids on top.
Arrange the éclairs on a large cake plate and serve.
